editorial.evidence: Read all 49 captured sections of the batch pipeline source (intro, interview guide, six deep-dive topics, cheat sheet and the five-part full design) and mapped each to the new structure in 90 item-level rows. The guide and full design repeated the sizing, architecture and 4 a.m. material; these were consolidated into eleven walkthrough steps that keep both versions' distinct details (the guide's 2k RPM, EU residency and 8k-token examples alongside the full design's eleven-axis table; the guide's Reliability and Operability targets merged into the full design's testable NFR table). Added teaching: a term list in the brief, an illustrative r-1042 record trace, a crash-point table for the write-checkpoint-ack order, an illustrative 4 a.m. rate calculation (7,640 rec/s needed vs 3,125 observed, assuming a midnight start) and a labelled illustrative cost price. Kept the source's attribution of the cost formula and compliance frameworks to a supplementary V2 author. The original worksheet was not part of the capture and is not imported; the local worksheet is labelled as an addition. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): the happy-path step 5 text listed checkpoint before the sink write, against the source's own write-then-checkpoint rule (data-plane figure, flow steps, tests, sixty-second close) → step 5 now teaches write first, then checkpoint, and the meta note was replaced by one neutral sentence saying the hashed figure labels step 5 by its checkpoint alone.
